msq440: nebular hypothesis nebular hypothesis is most widely accepted model in field of cosmogony to explain formation and evolution of solar system as well as other planetary systems it suggests that solar system formed from nebulous material theory was developed by immanuel kant and published in his allgemeine naturgeschichte und theorie des himmels universal natural history and theory of heavens published in 1755 originally applied to solar system process of planetary system formation is now thought to be at work throughout universe widely accepted modern variant of nebular hypothesis is solar nebular disk model sndm or solar nebular model it offered explanations for variety of properties of solar system including nearly circular and coplanar orbits of planets and their motion in same direction as sun s rotation some elements of nebular hypothesis are echoed in modern theories of planetary formation but most elements have been superseded
